headline: In AGI by 2028, the short path to capable robots makes factory wages and replacement work urgent concerns.
whatTheySay: Operators distinguish **2028 thinking AI** in planning from capable robots handling materials around 2031.
Many seek **written staffing terms**, paid safe training and actual vacancies before giving up current wages.
Some turn to **family, lenders or unions** when a quick income gap could outlast savings.
whatTheyThink: Many expect **machine hours or premiums** to disappear once capable robots reach the line.
A **small reserve** may not bridge rent or mortgage payments through a long search.
Even with savings, **posted safe jobs and adequate net pay** are uncertain; some planned technical paths face AI first.
howTheyFeel: **138 of 202** are alarmed in AGI by 2028, expecting major income loss.
Another **60 of 202** are anxious, often citing savings or local openings that buy some time.
**4 of 202** are panicked, with no reliable plan or buffer for the quick shift.

differences.text: Average worry is 4.03 for 72 thin-cushion profiles, versus 3.33 for 63 strong-cushion profiles (1 calm to 5 panicked).
Resistant profiles average 3.88 worry (68), versus 3.55 among adaptive profiles (67).
Late-stage profiles average 3.85 worry (40), compared with 3.65 among early-stage profiles (81).

least.name: Options to search
least.story: The 60 least worried remain anxious; 42 have strong cushions, giving many time to check posted work or paid training.

most.name: Long income gaps
most.story: The 142 alarmed or panicked profiles face major income risk; 70 have thin cushions, and many cannot cover a long search.

whatTheyDo.text: 163 of 202 consider changing jobs; Fatima Dubois would apply to a posted safe local loom if shifts fall and net pay covers bills.
109 of 202 plan to cut spending; Carlos Larsen would stop paid weekend outings if robot shifts fall.
93 of 202 plan retraining; Nora Nakamura would enrol in can inspection if offered a funded, paid, guarded, fitter-led place.
81 of 202 seek support; Fatima Alvarez agrees with her mother to use a back room if wages stop.
53 of 202 take collective action; Zoe Novak would join a union demonstration for notice and wages if called.

quotes.name: Fatima Dubois
quotes.text: Our savings are for living costs, not course fees that the plant ought to cover.

quotes.name: Carlos Larsen
quotes.text: We have less than a month saved, a mortgage and two children; I lie awake working out which payment could wait.

quotes.name: Colin Schmidt
quotes.text: My girlfriend Jess believes in me more than I do, and I'd hate to let her down.

thoughts.text: Capable robots could remove my factory role within a few years.
Thin savings could not carry a long loss of wages.
Savings or other local work cannot guarantee income after a factory wage loss.
My partner's income also looks exposed in the fast shift.
Thinking AI could take my skilled work before robots take the line.
